claims.text: Covering a massive area, the Place de la Concorde holds the title of the largest public square in all of Paris.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: It was originally designed in 1755 as an octagonal square named 'Place Louis XV', complete with a grand statue of the king.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Unlike most enclosed city squares, it is uniquely bordered by open space on three of its sides: the Champs-Élysées, the Tuileries garden, and the river Seine.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The square was dramatically renamed 'Place de la Révolution' following the historic events of 10 August 1792.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: During the Reign of Terror, it became the infamous site where King Louis XVI, Marie Antoinette, and many others were publicly guillotined.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The peaceful name 'Concorde' was later chosen to mark the reconciliation of the French people and encourage them to move past the bloodshed.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Today, the very center of the square is famously marked by a towering Egyptian obelisk that was originally brought from the Temple of Luxor.
claims.subject: self
